title: chunked-prefetch-and-eviction-throttle-for-kv-cache
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Introduces chunked prefetch to reduce head-of-line blocking and an eviction-throttle to smooth background reclaim IO; opt-in via feature flag. Improves p99 tail latency under hot cross-tenant workloads. No API changes.
commits: 3f8b2a1 - introduce chunked prefetcher and unit tests
b219d5a - hook prefetch into scheduler path and add batching hints
a9f0c33 - integration tests and bench fixtures
d4e0f12 - expose runtime flags and canary rollout config
e11b5a3 - fix race in allocator stats path (addressed CI flaky test)
description:
Context and motivation:
Large KV cache fetches are a frequent source of head-of-line blocking and IO bursts during eviction-driven reclaim. On multi-tenant inference workloads this shows up as sporadic p99 latency spikes and reduced sustained throughput when reclaim background work coincides with hot request batches.

Goal:
- Reduce H-o-L blocking caused by large contiguous KV fetches by breaking them into smaller prefetch chunks that interleave with the request execution path.
- Smooth background reclaim/eviction IO by adding an eviction-throttle that rate-limits eviction work based on current SLO pressure and a small token-bucket tied to per-GPU IO budget.
- Surface scheduler/batcher hints so the serving runtime can avoid issuing fetch+evict storms while maintaining high throughput for short requests.

What this PR changes (high level):
- pkg/kv/cache/prefetcher.go: new chunked prefetcher that fetches blocks in configurable chunk sizes and yields to the scheduler between chunks. Prefetcher uses an adaptive chunk-size heuristic (defaults tuned via canary) that grows/shrinks based on observed fetch latency and KV hit ratio.
- pkg/kv/allocator/eviction_throttle.go: eviction-throttle controller implementing a small token-bucket and backoff policy. Throttle is SLO-aware: it samples request latency percentiles published by the serving runtime and reduces eviction drain rate when tail latency increases.
- pkg/serving/scheduler/batcher.go: adds prefetch-yield hooks to allow continuous-batching to interleave I/O with token processing, reducing stall windows for other batches. Also plumbs a batch-priority hint that lowers eviction allowed rate while high-priority user batches are in-flight.
- cmd/redwood/flags.go + config/defaults.go: new feature flags and default parameters for canary: chunk_size_pages, max_chunks_per_request, eviction_tokens_per_second, slo_latency_threshold_ms. Defaults off for global rollout; enabled for canary nodepool.
- tests/unit/prefetcher_test.go and tests/integration/prefetch_eviction_test.go: coverage for chunked fetch ordering, interleaving correctness, and throttle behavior under synthetic SLO violation.
- bench/kv_prefetch_bench.yaml: bench config used for local and CI regression tests.

Design notes and rationale:
- Chunking vs. full fetch: empirical runs in benchmark lab showed that breaking 256-page fetches into 8x32-page chunks reduced median stall time by ~38% and p99 by ~22% under mixed workloads because it gives the runtime scheduler opportunities to schedule other small batches.
- Eviction-throttle instead of disable reclaim: simply pausing reclaim leads to memory pressure spikes. Throttle lets reclaim continue at a controlled rate so long-running background compaction does not synchronize across GPUs and cause IO bursts.
- SLO feedback loop: throttle uses a conservative low-pass filter on p95/p99 signals to avoid oscillation. We also emit internal metrics (prefetch.chunk_count, evict.throttle_tokens, evict.drain_rate) for alerting and tuning.

Benchmarks (canary nodepool, synthetic mixed workload):
- p50 latency: -6% (improvement)
- p95 latency: -14%
- p99 latency: -22%
- sustained throughput: +7%
- Background IO variance (stddev): -45%
Notes: numbers aggregated from 6 runs, canary enabled with defaults. Full benchmark scripts are in bench/ and were run with bench infra id bench-20241107-12.

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests added for prefetcher and throttle. Integration test simulates SLO violation and asserts eviction drain rate reduces and that in-flight batches are not stalled.
- CI initially failed flakily on integration test (race in allocator stats). I added a small synchronization in allocator stats update and reran CI; all green.

Review conversation (high level):
- Aaron Liu: "Can we show the cost regression for cold-starts? Chunking could add small extra latency if the first chunk misses and subsequent chunks are needed."
  - Priya: "Added a benchmark for cold fetch penalty and tuned initial chunk size. Cold-start p50 increased by <2ms for very large multi-page misses; we consider this acceptable vs tail improvements. Documented in bench/README and release notes."
- Camille Dubois: "Please add metrics and a flag to disable chunking per node. Also add a rollout plan for Dedicated customers."
  - Priya: "Added metrics and cmd flags. Default remains off for global; enabled on canary nodepool. Dedicated will get opt-in via runtime config."
- Jorge Ramirez: "CI showed a data-race in allocator stats on the first run; please fix and re-run."
  - Priya: "Fixed by moving stats write to a single updater goroutine and added unit test to surface regression. CI green afterwards."

Operational notes and rollout:
- Feature gated: default off at global scale. Canary nodepool in us-west-2 enabled for 2 weeks under monitoring.
- New metrics: prefretch.chunk_size, prefetch.chunks_per_req, evict.throttle_tokens, evict.drain_rate, kv.prefetch_yields. Dashboards updated in observability-pack (PR referenced in Linear ENG-6324).
- Alerting: added a burn-rate style alert if evict.drain_rate drops while p99 latency climbs > 15% for >5m.
